Seminar Title:

Return Seminar: Impact of spray and freeze drying on physicochemical and functional characteristics of encapsulated custard apple peel extract: A waste valorization study

Seminar Type:

Speaker Name:

Shubham Mahendra Nimbkar

11 Nov 2026 16.45

Contact:

Abstract:

Growing emphasis on sustainable food processing and circular bioeconomy has increased interest in valorization of food processing waste streams. Custard apple peel a rich source of bioactive compounds, largely remain underutilized. In this work, the ethanolic extracts of custard peel were encapsulated in a polysaccharide-based (maltodextrin+gum acacia) and protein- polysaccharide-based (Whey protein+pectin) matrix through spray and freeze drying. The prepared encapsulates were characterized for physicochemical and functional properties, microstructure and core-wall interactions. Spray dried encapsulates showed higher moisture content, while freeze dried samples demonstrated lower water activity and higher yield. All encapsulated samples reported higher encapsulation efficiency in the range of (~96-99%) with freeze dried maltodextrin+gum acacia sample reporting highest encapsulation efficiency (99.02 ± 0.38%) owing to minimal thermal degradation. Consequently, total phenolic (10.78 ± 0.34 mg GAE/g) and flavonoid content (7.63 ± 0.27 mg QE/g) and antioxidant activity (61.44 ± 1.35%) was observed higher in freeze dried encapsulates. Microstructure analysis revealed smooth spherical particles in spray dried encapsulates as opposed to flake-like particles in freeze dried ones. FTIR analysis shows successful encapsulation of phenolic compounds. Overall, this work demonstrates successful encapsulation of custard apple peel extracts with a strong potential for development of a nutraceutical product from fruit processing waste.
